verdict_reason: Harvest's own help center states that API access is included with every subscription, including free and trial accounts, so credentials are self-serve with no sales contact or review. The V2 authentication docs show both a Personal Access Token (sent as a bearer token) and a full OAuth2 authorization-code flow for multi-user integrations. The API is read-write across account data with permissions mirroring the UI, which is sufficient breadth for useful actions.
open_questions: Name collision: https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/docs/authentication and https://help.getharvest.com/... co-occur; the Greenhouse 'Harvest v3' API at harvest.greenhouse.io is a different product and its auth/MCP details (including the Greenhouse MCP server) were excluded from this record.
platform.harvestapp.com pages (the 'Integrate your app with Harvest' partner platform) rendered as JS shells / sign-in screens, so any partner-program requirements documented there could not be read.
Rate-limit numbers were not in the fetched evidence; the support article only points to the API overview documentation for throttling limits.
No evidence of webhooks/event callbacks or a sandbox/test environment was found in the fetched pages; both are recorded as not_found rather than false.
No vendor-operated or credible community MCP server for Harvest (getharvest.com) was found; MCP registry results were empty.
No fetched page explicitly labels the API as 'REST'; the type was inferred from documented HTTPS JSON endpoints (e.g. https://api.harvestapp.com/v2/users/me), hence low confidence.
The Ruby/PHP/Python/Java 'wrappers' are only described as linked libraries in Harvest's code samples; whether they are vendor-maintained or third-party is unclear.
Exact endpoint/resource count for API v2 is not enumerated in the fetched pages.

audit.exclusion_reason: Greenhouse Harvest v3 recruiting API — different product from Harvest (getharvest.com).
audit.metadata_note: S6/S7/S8 and the pricing page are on vendor domains (help.getharvest.com, support.getharvest.com, getharvest.com) but were flagged OFFICIAL: no by the fetcher; they were treated as vendor documentation and corroborated by the input description pointing to help.getharvest.com/api-v2.
